data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs_

**Class:** Quaternary ammonium antimuscarinics (anticholinergics) — poor CNS penetration

## Mechanism of action
- Block muscarinic (M3) receptors on eccrine sweat glands (sympathetic cholinergic innervation) → reduced sweating

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Hyperhidrosis (generalised, craniofacial, compensatory, palmoplantar) — oral glycopyrrolate or propantheline
- Topical glycopyrronium tosylate 2.4% cloth (axillary hyperhidrosis, approved USA), 1% cream (Europe), iontophoresis with glycopyrrolate solution for refractory palmar hyperhidrosis
- Drooling (sialorrhoea), anaesthetic premedication

## Dose & formulations
- Glycopyrrolate 1–2 mg once or twice daily (titrate); propantheline 15 mg three times daily
- Topical cloth once daily to both axillae

## Adverse effects
- Dry mouth (most common), blurred vision (mydriasis), constipation, urinary retention, tachycardia, heat intolerance (risk of heat stroke)
- Topical: local irritation, transient mydriasis if touched to eyes

## Contraindications
- Glaucoma, myasthenia gravis, obstructive uropathy, paralytic ileus, severe ulcerative colitis, tachyarrhythmia

## Drug interactions
- Other anticholinergics (TCAs, antihistamines); potassium chloride tablets (GI lesions)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Limited data — avoid.

## Viva points
- Quaternary amine — fewer CNS effects than atropine
- Hyperhidrosis treatment ladder: topical aluminium chloride → iontophoresis → botulinum toxin → oral anticholinergics → sympathectomy

_Sources: Khopkar (Glycopyrrolate and propantheline bromide); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
